method: Whole-file manual reading of DarkMode.h and cpp,450 lines; pinned bytes verified. No native UI execution.
findings: Dark mode combines configured preference, Windows theme registry value, version/build capability and high-contrast state. High contrast disables custom dark mode; system colors are used when dark mode is disabled. This is source policy, not an accessibility qualification.

Undocumented uxtheme ordinals133/135 are runtime-resolved; ordinal135 is called through an older bool signature before build18362 and preferred-mode enum thereafter. Compatibility across actual Windows builds was not executed.

AdjustControls applies themes recursively and updates list/RichEdit colors, then requests frame change. Most theme/DWM return values are ignored except E_INVALIDARG fallback for immersive dark mode attribute. Partial adjustment is not reported as failure.

Enhanced button support is determined by registry build/revision and cached in a function-static bool. This source records a capability threshold; no external verification of the referenced update or live system behavior was performed.
Menu label buffer is fixed256 wchar_t and GetMenuItemInfo result is not checked; unusually long menu text may be truncated. Owner-drawn menu items fall back to DefWindowProc.

LightenBitmap rejects nonpositive dimensions and checks width*height*4 overflow before allocating. GetDIBits is accepted on any nonzero scanline count rather than verifying full requested height, and SetDIBits result is ignored. Partial-transfer behavior remains untested.

Bitmap transform modifies only BGR channels, leaving the fourth byte unchanged; invert maps255-channel and lightening uses sqrt gamma LUT. No image fidelity, alpha semantics or performance measurement established.
Global dark-mode state and shared static brushes are unsynchronized; normal GUI-thread ownership is assumed rather than proven for arbitrary concurrent callers.
limits: No Windows version, high-contrast, theme switching, menu, bitmap transfer or GUI tests executed.
No foreign production code adopted; native pHash investigation deferred. Global completed repository count remains147/500.
